# awesome-health-ai-evals

A map of health benchmarks and evaluation frameworks for generative-AI chatbots, with attention to where the evidence comes from: low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) as well as high-income ones.

This is an exploratory catalog, not a systematic review. Screening and data extraction were done with LLM assistance, and some facts may be wrong; each entry records how confident the extraction is. See [How this list was built](#how-this-list-was-built) and [Known gaps](#known-gaps).

**994 entries.** Item origin: 566 global or unknown, 226 high-income only, 177 native LMIC, 21 adapted, 4 translated only. Of the 177 native LMIC entries, 103 have items from China alone; 6 entries include items from a low-income country.

Columns: **Item origin** is where the questions or conversations came from. **Income group** is the World Bank group of those countries (pinned in `data/countries.csv`). **Method**: MCQ = multiple choice or exact match; metric = automatic text metric; LLM judge = rubric scored by a language model; expert rating = human expert rating; multi-turn = simulated patient or dialogue; real users = scored on real users' conversations.

## Constructs, site, and skills

- **Constructs.** Agents extracted the evaluation terms each judged benchmark and framework scores outputs on ([`terms/`](terms/)), with verbatim definitions where the source gives them. These were clustered and turned into a taxonomy of constructs (what evaluations judge) by a proposer agent and a challenger agent with a low-resource primary-care lens; see [`taxonomy/`](taxonomy/) and [`docs/taxonomy.md`](docs/taxonomy.md).
- **Site.** A browsable catalog with a world map, heatmaps, a construct explorer, and side-by-side comparison is built from the same files (`uv run scripts/build_site.py`, output in `site/dist`).
- **Skills.** [`skills/`](skills/) holds four Claude Code skills, installable as a plugin: `find-health-benchmarks`, `adapt-benchmark-rubric`, `score-transcripts-with-rubric`, and `run-open-benchmark`. Install with `/plugin marketplace add littlehifive/awesome-health-ai-evals`, then `/plugin install health-ai-evals@health-ai-evals`.

## How this list was built

Searches of OpenAlex, paperclip (arXiv, medRxiv, PMC, and an abstracts corpus), Hugging Face, and GitHub returned 27,750 unique records (queries in [`search/queries.yaml`](search/queries.yaml), hit counts in [`search/log.csv`](search/log.csv)). The OpenAlex search also followed citations of anchor benchmarks and the reference lists of surveys. A small model screened 27,837 titles and abstracts, keeping anything uncertain, and a larger model re-screened what it kept with a stricter prompt ([`search/screening.csv`](search/screening.csv)). Claude agents then read the full text of the remaining candidates ([`search/candidates.csv`](search/candidates.csv)) and wrote each entry or logged why not ([`search/extraction/`](search/extraction/)). Decisions and scope are in [`docs/plan.md`](docs/plan.md).

## Known gaps

- **English-language search only.** Benchmarks described only in other languages are likely missing.
- **Practice-built evaluations are undercounted.** Eval sets that implementers build for their own chatbots are rarely published. If you have one you can share, even as a description, please open an issue.
- **LLM-assisted screening and extraction.** Expect some misclassified records and wrong facts. Corrections are welcome.

## Contributing

Open an issue to add a benchmark or correct an entry. Each entry is a YAML file in `entries/`; the fields are described in [`schema/README.md`](schema/README.md), and `uv run scripts/validate.py` checks them.
